Monash Health is a great place to work
Monash Health is Victoria’s largest and most comprehensive health service. For more than 170 years, Monash Health and its predecessors have provided safe, high-quality healthcare and service for people at every life stage. Monash Health team members care deeply about the community and about one another. 
As a leading academic health service, Monash Health is committed to the integration of research, teaching and training into everyday practice.  
To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos: monashhealth.org/careers.
 
About Monash Doctors 

To help grow your career, there are more than 1,900 Junior and 1,700 Senior Doctors at Monash Health in over 200 medical specialties. We offer unparallel opportunities in Victoria's largest & most clinically diverse teaching health service. 
 
About General Medicine 

Monash Health General Medicine is a busy department that delivers a vast volume of clinical services in inpatient and ambulatory settings, with inpatient activity at three major hospital campuses namely Casey Hospital, Dandenong Hospital, and Monash Medical Centre. The General Medicine department fosters strong partnerships with every other medical department as well as a range of external stakeholders, in order to understand and adapt to meeting community needs upon a constantly changing healthcare landscape in Victoria. 
 
General Medicine engages with the organisation’s education, research and clinical governance programs, to promote continuous improvement of the standard of care. In particular, the department is defined by a culture of reflective learning and interdisciplinary teamwork. 
 
About the Role 

The General Medicine Registrar role delivers services through rotational placements at multiple campuses of Monash Health. Beyond service delivery, the Registrar role is designed to participate in activities that contribute to the standard of the health service, such as research, teaching, and quality improvement. 
 
At Monash Health General Medicine, the Registrar is to role model strong interdisciplinary collaboration that is based on effective communication. The professional development of the Registrar is to be self-driven. 
 
About You 

What you need: 
•	Medical qualification which is recognised for registration by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) 
•	Demonstrated ability to work cohesively as part of interdisciplinary teams 
•	Clinical experience commensurate with the standards required by Monash Health for medical registrar practice 
 
Mandatory requirements of the role: 
•	Current drivers licence 
•	Capacity to deliver care in the hospital (at all Monash Health campuses) and in the ambulatory setting 
•	Working rights in Australia 
•	Two (2) completed referee reports (see below) 
 
 
For any enquiries, please contact A/Prof Gary Yip, Service Medical Director – General Medicine via email at Gary.Yip@monashhealth.org. 
 
 
Our Culture and Values 

At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 
 
Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 
 
You’ll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 
 
We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 
 
We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.  
 
How to Apply

Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system.
 
Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

Grounded Construction Group is currently looking to recruit an experienced and qualified Bulldozer Operator to join their team in Muchea WA.


The Bulldozer Operator is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of bulldozers to undertake bulk earthworks, clearing, site preparation, material spreading, pushing, ripping and final shaping activities across construction, civil, mining infrastructure and non-process infrastructure (NPI) projects. The role is responsible for achieving production targets while maintaining compliance with company, client and legislative requirements.

The successful candidate will need to undertake and possess:

-  Operate bulldozers safely and efficiently to undertake bulk earthworks, site preparation and construction activities. 
-  Clear vegetation, topsoil and unsuitable material from work areas in accordance with project requirements. 
-  Push, spread and level soil, rock, gravel and other construction materials. 
-  Carry out ripping, backfilling and ground preparation activities. 
-  Construct and maintain building pads, hardstands, access roads and haul roads. 
-  Perform final trim works to specified design levels and project tolerances where required. 
-  Read and work from construction drawings, survey pegs, GPS machine control systems and supervisor instructions.
-  Conduct daily pre-start inspections and complete required plant inspection documentation. 
-  Monitor equipment performance and report faults or maintenance requirements promptly. 
-  Carry out routine servicing, lubrication and minor maintenance within competency limits. 
-  Participate in pre-start meetings, toolbox meetings and safety interactions. 
-  Operate safely around personnel, mobile plant, underground services and fixed infrastructure. 
-  Maintain compliance with Grounded, client and statutory safety requirements. 
-  Complete required plant logs, inspection records and production documentation accurately. 
-  Assist with site establishment and other construction activities where required. 
-  Maintain housekeeping standards around work areas and equipment. 
-  Contribute to achieving project production, quality and safety objectives. 


Skills and Abilities:
-  Relevant qualification equivalent to AQF Certificate II or Certificate III, or equivalent industry experience. 
-  Minimum one (1) year relevant experience operating bulldozers. 
-  Current Driver’s Licence (HR – MC Role Dependant) 
-  Operating SOA 
-  Operating VOC (2 years validity)


Salary range is $75,000 - $85,000pa commensurate with experience.

Fulltime Position available

Applications open on 20th July 2026 and closes on 20th August 2026

If you are interested in this role APPLY now. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted
